title: RelationVGGT : Visual Geometry Transformers for 3D Spatial Relation Segmentation
claim: A frozen-foundation-model backbone fuses semantic and geometric features, conditions on a subject mask, and decodes text-matched relation segmentation across views.
layout: 1 wide panel, left-to-right flow, multi-view inputs on left, outputs on right
description: A single wide left-to-right architecture diagram. At left, a stack of multi-view indoor room photos feeds two frozen (snowflake-marked) foundation model blocks, a green 2D VFM and a blue 3D VFM. Their tokens, drawn as overlapping blue and green squares, enter a tall purple Input Mixer. The mixed tokens, with a black subject mask injected via a green arrow, pass through a green Relation Transformer made of N stacked transformer blocks. An orange Mask Decoder then produces per-view relation maps R1, R2 and R3. Above, a speech bubble reading 'What is <mask> lying on?' feeds a frozen BERT block. Its text embedding is combined by circled-multiply symbols with the relation maps. The result is a segmentation overlay compared with GT through a loss L. A point decoder at the bottom produces a 3D point cloud and a 3D visualization.
caption: Overview of RelationVGGT. Multi-view images are encoded by frozen 2D and 3D visual foundation models and fused via an input mixer. The subject mask conditions the relation transformer, whose output is decoded into per-view relation feature maps. The target object is segmented via feature--text similarity with the BERT-encoded relational query.
abstract: Recent advances in 3D reconstruction have progressed from per-scene optimization to feed-forward inference, and semantic scene understanding has followed suit -- yet existing methods remain confined to object-centric perception, neglecting spatial relations between objects. We formulate 3D spatial relation segmentation in a feed-forward, pose-free multi-view setting: given a visually specified subject and a relational text query, the model segments the target across views without receiving its category name. To this end, we propose RelationVGGT, a novel feed-forward framework that integrates semantic features from a visual foundation model with geometry-aware representations from a 3D geometry foundation model and leverages a relation transformer for subject-conditioned, cross-view relation prediction -- requiring neither per-scene optimization nor known camera poses. We additionally provide a fully automated annotation pipeline built on ScanNet++ with VLMs and LLMs, enabling scalable training data generation for this new task.
